Alex —

Thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; attaching a compact SIG response pack and a short example retention policy. See attachments: redwood_SIG_answers_medsys_20270425.pdf and s3-retention-policy-example.txt.

1) Hosted (default): request/response logs (enterprise-level prompt traces) are ephemeral by default — retained for 24 hours for routing, debugging, and abuse detection. Customers may enable longer retention for observability; that requires an explicit config and billing change.

2) Dedicated: logs remain in the customer-dedicated environment; default retention is 30 days but can be configured by the customer/team that owns the Dedicated capacity. Redwood supports an opt-in only model for using customer prompts to improve our models. We do not train or fine-tune hosted customer content unless the customer explicitly agrees in writing and the contract lists that permission.

3) Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood control plane can be configured to not receive any prompt-level payloads. In on-prem deployments, customer retains full control of logs and lifecycle.

Attestation (summary): Redwood does not use customer prompt or response content for model training by default. Any training on customer data requires explicit, documented opt-in and is subject to contract-level approvals and data processing agreements.

I'll loop in Soojin and Evelyn for a formal attestation doc and SOC/SIG evidence links.

Action items:

- Evelyn: can you provide an example of the Dedicated retention config and a short note on Private deployments?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Hi Alex —

Quick answers to Alex's follow-ups:

- Hosted opt-in retention: Customers can configure retention windows via the Console (per-tenant settings). We persist logs in Redwood-managed storage when customers opt in; retention settings are visible in the Console and can be exported. We do not currently provide an immutable write-once archive by default, but we can support export to customer-owned storage for compliance customers as part of Dedicated/Private engagements.

- Dedicated storage & KMS: By default, Dedicated deployments store logs in Redwood-managed buckets in the customer’s dedicated project; encryption keys are customer-specific and managed using the customer's KMS where requested (we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated). For strict compliance customers we recommend configuring customer-owned S3 buckets and customer KMS.

- One-sentence attestation (suitable for SIG): "Redwood Inference does not use customer prompts or responses to train models or improve model weights unless the customer explicitly opts in via contract; any such use is subject to documented consent and controls."

Attachments included in the final pack: a compact attestation PDF, SOC2 summary (public), and an example S3 lifecycle snippet. Evelyn — can you drop the Dedicated config snippet for MedSys?

Regards,
Soojin Lee
